headline: Find gaps in the union of everyone's working intervals
statement: Each employee has sorted, nonoverlapping working intervals. Return sorted finite positive-length intervals during which every employee is free. Exclude the unbounded time before all work and after all work. Input and output intervals have start and end attributes.
constraints: 1 to 50 employees, each with 1 to 50 working intervals.
Each employee's own intervals are sorted and do not overlap.
intuition: Everyone is free precisely where nobody is working. Flatten all busy intervals, sort by start, and sweep their union. If a new interval starts strictly after the farthest busy endpoint, the space between is a common free interval.
approach: Flatten intervals into start/end pairs and sort.
Initialize busy_end from the first interval.
For each later interval, emit [busy_end,start] only when start > busy_end.
Extend busy_end to the larger endpoint.
correctness: After each interval, busy_end is the right boundary of the processed busy union's final component. Sorted starts ensure that no unseen interval can cover a gap preceding the current start. A strictly later start therefore identifies an exact finite free component; overlapping or touching intervals extend the busy union without a gap.
bruteForce: Inspect every time coordinate and test all employees, impractical for endpoints up to 100 million. A heap merge of the already sorted employee lists can reduce sorting cost when employee count is small.

complexity.explanation: N is the total number of busy intervals; flattening and sorting dominate.

pitfalls: Touching intervals create no positive-length gap.
Keep the maximum endpoint when intervals nest.
Do not return infinite leading or trailing free intervals.
